title: Synthesis and characterization of poly(styrene-co-divinylbenzene) and nanomagnetite structures
author: Reis, de Sousa, et al.

steps.title: Gather reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect all chemicals and apparatus: Styrene (≥99 %), divinylbenzene (55 %), benzoyl peroxide (≥65 % anhydrous, ≤25 % water), trisodium phosphate (96 %), calcium chloride (≥93 %, ≤7 mm), sodium dodecyl sulfate (≥99 %), 10 % (m/v) NaOH solution, deionized water, 2 N HCl, absolute ethanol, magnetite nanoparticles (97 %, 50–100 nm), oleic acid, ultrasonic bath, round‑bottom flask, heating mantle, magnetic stirrer, OptiMax™ 1001 thermostat reactor, vacuum filtration setup, oven (40 °C).

steps.title: Wash styrene and divinylbenzene
steps.instruction: Remove inhibitor from monomers by washing with 10 % NaOH (m/v) and then with distilled water.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 36 mL of Styrene and 1.44 mL of DVB (obtain 1.44 mL by pipetting 2.62 mL of 55 % DVB solution) into a decanting funnel.
Add an equal volume of 10 % NaOH to each monomer, shake, let the denser phase separate, and discard; repeat this NaOH wash three times.
Wash each monomer three times with distilled water using a 2:1 water‑to‑monomer volume ratio (twice the monomer volume), shaking and discarding the aqueous layer each time.
Collect the washed monomers and keep them protected from air.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Make the aqueous phase (AP) containing calcium phosphate precipitate, calcium chloride, sodium phosphate and surfactant.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1.85 g calcium chloride and 1.82 g sodium phosphate (Na3PO4).
Dissolve each solid separately in distilled water, then combine the two solutions.
Add 0.02 g sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) to the combined solution.
Adjust the total volume of the aqueous phase to 120 mL (≈1.43 % m/v Ca3(PO4)2 in AP).

steps.title: Prepare organic phase
steps.instruction: Make the organic phase (OP) with washed monomers and initiator.

substeps.instruction: Measure 30 mL total volume for the organic phase (OP).
Add the washed Styrene (36 mL) and DVB (1.44 mL) to a clean container.
Add 1.50 g benzoyl peroxide (BPO) (4 % m/v of OP) to the monomers and mix gently.

steps.title: Add magnetite (direct method) – optional
steps.instruction: If incorporating magnetite without oleic acid, disperse it before polymerization.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 3.3 g magnetite nanoparticles (10 % m/m of OP).
Place the magnetite in the reactor vessel and ultrasonicate for 3 min to obtain a uniform dispersion.

steps.title: Prepare oleic‑acid‑coated magnetite – optional
steps.instruction: If using oleic‑acid‑treated magnetite, prepare it before polymerization.

substeps.instruction: Add 150 mL deionized water to a round‑bottom flask and heat to 65 °C with a heating mantle.
Add 3.3 g magnetite nanoparticles to the hot water.
Gradually add 50 mL oleic acid while stirring.
Continue stirring at 65 °C for 30 min.
Add enough absolute ethanol to the mixture to aid phase separation, allow the mixture to stand, then decant the aqueous layer.
Filter off excess water, and let the oleic‑acid‑coated magnetite dry at room temperature until all water is removed.

steps.title: Load reactor with phases
steps.instruction: Introduce the prepared phases into the polymerization reactor.

substeps.instruction: Place the OptiMax™ 1001 thermostat reactor on the bench.
Add the 120 mL aqueous phase (AP) to the reactor vessel.
Add the 30 mL organic phase (OP) containing monomers (and BPO) to the same reactor.
If magnetite is to be incorporated, add either the directly dispersed magnetite (Step 5) or the oleic‑acid‑treated magnetite (Step 6) now.

steps.title: Run polymerization program
steps.instruction: Execute the temperature‑and‑agitation schedule in the automated reactor.

substeps.instruction: Step 1: Set agitation to 900 rpm, maintain at 25 °C for 3 h.
Step 2: Increase temperature to 82 °C while keeping agitation at 900 rpm (heating ramp; duration ~2 h until temperature stabilises).
Step 3: Hold at 82 °C, reduce agitation to 500 rpm, and maintain for 5 h.

steps.title: Post‑polymerization work‑up
steps.instruction: Recover, wash, and dry the polymeric microparticles.

substeps.instruction: Allow the reactor to cool to room temperature (25 °C) and switch off the instrument.
Open the reactor and remove the reaction mixture.
Vacuum‑filter the solid product and wash the cake with hot water.
Transfer the wet solid to a beaker, add 2 N hydrochloric acid, stir for 1 h, then filter.
Rinse the solid with absolute ethanol, stir for 2 h, and vacuum‑filter again.
Place the filtered solid in an oven set to 40 °C and dry for 24 h.
